# *stareal*

Spatial-temporal areal estimation from survey data

*stareal* fits a Bayesian space-time model to binomial survey data, such
as the prevalence of a drug-resistance marker, at an areal level:
administrative units, or any other set of polygons. Time runs in regular
steps of your choosing, such as months, quarters or years. The model
estimates prevalence in every area and time step, including the many
with no surveys, by borrowing strength from neighbouring areas and
nearby times, and gives the uncertainty of every estimate. Regional and
national summaries are made from the joint posterior, so their
uncertainty is right too.

*stareal* is built for data that are sparse relative to the space-time
grid: hundreds of areas, decades of months, and surveys in a small
fraction of the area-time cells. Standard areal software carries a
latent value for every cell, surveyed or not, which becomes heavy at
fine time resolution. *stareal* integrates the unsurveyed cells out
exactly and fits the model to the surveyed cells alone. Its cost depends
on the number of surveys, not on the size of the map. The full surface
is then rebuilt from each posterior draw. Inference is by MCMC
throughout, with no approximation of the posterior.

![Predicted prevalence of the chloroquine-resistance marker crt K76T
across the eight IGAD countries, from the first
tutorial.](reference/figures/hero-crt76t.png)

Predicted prevalence of the chloroquine-resistance marker crt K76T
across the eight IGAD countries, from the first tutorial.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mrc-ide/stareal")
```

## A first map

``` r
library(stareal)
iso3 <- c("DJI", "ERI", "ETH", "KEN", "SOM", "SSD", "SDN", "UGA")      # the eight IGAD countries
adm1 <- sf::st_as_sf(geodata::gadm(iso3, level = 1, path = tempdir(), resolution = 2))
adm1 <- adm1[adm1$ENGTYPE_1 != "Water body", ]                          # lakes are not places
fr <- areal_frame(adm1, id = "GID_1", groups = c(country = "COUNTRY"),
                  link_within = "country")                               # areas and their neighbours
tf <- time_frame(1989, 2024, "month")                                    # the time grid
d  <- areal_data(igad_crt76t, fr, tf, y = "positive", k = "tested",
                 coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), date = "collection_day")
fit <- fit_areal(d)                                                      # MCMC, chains in parallel
diagnose(fit)                                                            # convergence of every parameter
pr <- predict(fit, groups = "country")                                   # every area-month, and countries
plot(pr, time = "2024-01")
```

## Tutorials

|  |  |
|----|----|
| [**1. Mapping crt K76T in the Greater Horn of Africa**](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/crt76t.md) | From a STAVE data object to monthly maps, country trends and probability statements. |
| [**2. Rare and emerging markers: k13 R561H in East Africa**](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/k13-561h.md) | Mostly-zero data, exceedance probabilities, and when to doubt the map. |
| [**3. Covariates**](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/covariates.md) | Covariates by area, by time and by both: building the tables and reading the coefficients. |
| [**4. Cross-validation and model comparison**](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/crossval.md) | Which model predicts held-out surveys best, and is it calibrated? |
| [**5. Simulate, fit, check**](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/simulation.md) | Data simulated from known parameters: does the fit recover the truth? |

New to *stareal*? Start with tutorial 1. The
[**Method**](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/method.md) page
explains the model, why it is fitted the way it is, and how.

## Citation

Verity, R. *stareal*: spatial-temporal areal estimation from survey
data. R package, <https://github.com/mrc-ide/stareal>.

# Package index

## Space and time

- [`areal_frame()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/areal_frame.md)
  : Build a spatial frame
- [`areal_lattice()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/areal_lattice.md)
  : A regular lattice frame
- [`plot(`*`<stareal_frame>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/plot.stareal_frame.md)
  : Map a frame and its graph
- [`time_frame()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/time_frame.md)
  : Build a time frame
- [`time_index()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/time_index.md)
  : Map dates to time steps

## Data

- [`areal_data()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/areal_data.md)
  : Attach survey data to a frame
- [`plot(`*`<stareal_data>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/plot.stareal_data.md)
  : Plot survey data
- [`simulate_areal()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/simulate_areal.md)
  : Simulate survey data from the model

## Fitting

- [`fit_areal()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/fit_areal.md)
  : Fit the space-time areal model
- [`trend()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/trend.md) : A
  linear trend in time
- [`areal_priors()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/areal_priors.md)
  : Priors for an areal model
- [`mcmc_control()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/mcmc_control.md)
  : Settings for the MCMC sampler
- [`summary(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/summary.stareal_fit.md)
  : Summarise a fit
- [`diagnose()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/diagnose.md)
  : Check convergence and mixing of a fit
- [`plot(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/plot.stareal_fit.md)
  : Trace plots of a fit
- [`as_draws(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/as_draws.stareal_fit.md)
  [`as_draws_array(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/as_draws.stareal_fit.md)
  [`as_draws_df(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/as_draws.stareal_fit.md)
  [`as_draws_matrix(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/as_draws.stareal_fit.md)
  [`as_draws_list(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/as_draws.stareal_fit.md)
  [`as_draws_rvars(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/as_draws.stareal_fit.md)
  : Posterior draws of a fit

## Prediction and checking

- [`predict(`*`<stareal_fit>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/predict.stareal_fit.md)
  : Predict the full area-time surface from a fit
- [`plot(`*`<stareal_pred>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/plot.stareal_pred.md)
  : Plot predictions
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<stareal_pred>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/as.data.frame.stareal_pred.md)
  : Predictions as a data frame
- [`st_as_sf(`*`<stareal_pred>`*`)`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/st_as_sf.stareal_pred.md)
  : Predictions as polygons
- [`crossval()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/crossval.md)
  : Cross-validate a fit
- [`compare_cv()`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/reference/compare_cv.md)
  : Compare cross-validated models

# Articles

### Tutorials

Each tutorial answers one question with real or simulated data, from
start to finish.

- [1. Mapping crt K76T in the Greater Horn of
  Africa](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/crt76t.md):

  From a STAVE data object to monthly maps, country trends and
  probability statements: the chloroquine-resistance marker crt K76T
  across the eight IGAD countries, 1989-2024.

- [2. Rare and emerging markers: k13 R561H in East
  Africa](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/k13-561h.md):

  Mapping a marker that most surveys never find: the artemisinin
  partial-resistance mutation k13 R561H, from Rwanda into north-western
  Tanzania and south-western Uganda.

- [3.
  Covariates](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/covariates.md):

  Covariates by area, by time step, and by both: how to build the
  tables, how to read the coefficients, and what happens when the data
  cannot inform one.

- [4. Cross-validation and model
  comparison](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/crossval.md):

  Which model predicts held-out surveys best, and are its intervals
  calibrated? Random and spatial cross-validation, and comparing models
  on the same folds.

- [5. Simulate, fit,
  check](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/simulation.md):

  Data simulated from known parameters at the survey design of tutorial
  1: does the fit recover the truth, and are its intervals honest?

### Method

- [Method](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/articles/method.md):

  The model, why it can be fitted on the observed cells only, the
  sampler, and how predictions and group summaries are made.
